title: Securing AI Services in Applications

header.html: Request and manage access to AI services (2.3.1); use data privacy controls to transmit data to AI services (2.3.2); filter and control AI model inputs and outputs (2.3.3); secure AI agent interactions (2.3.4); protect sensitive content in monitoring logs during AI interactions (2.3.5)
the official AWS Developer Associate (DVA-C03) exam guide, Task 2.3 (new in DVA-C03)

toc.title: Data privacy in transit and use
Filtering inputs and outputs: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails

html:
1Request and manage access

Control What it does
Model access Access to a foundation model must be requested or enabled for the account [Verify live]
IAM permissions Grant bedrock:InvokeModel (and related actions) only to the roles that need it, scoped to specific models
Least privilege Separate roles for development, testing and production
Service control Organization policies can allow or deny models or Regions

2Data privacy in transit and use

Control What it does
VPC endpoint (AWS PrivateLink) Application traffic to the AI service stays on the AWS network, not the public internet
Encryption in transit TLS for every call
No training on your data Inputs and outputs sent to Bedrock are not used to train the base models; confirm and document this [Verify live]
Minimize data Send only what is needed; redact PII before sending
Exam tip

. "Keep traffic to the AI service off the public internet" = an interface VPC endpoint (PrivateLink).

3Filtering inputs and outputs: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails

Guardrails apply policies to prompts and responses [Verify live]:

Policy What it does
Content filters Block harmful categories in input and output
Prompt attack filter Detect jailbreaks and prompt injection in the input
Denied topics Block subjects you define, matched by meaning
Word filters Block exact words and phrases (and a profanity list)
Sensitive information filters Detect PII (and custom patterns) and block or mask it
Contextual grounding Check that a response is grounded in the source

The ApplyGuardrail API applies a guardrail to any text, without calling a model, so you can protect other models or your own content.

Exam tip

. Prompt injection is an attack in the input; the defense is the guardrail's prompt attack filter plus treating model output as untrusted. Mask PII = sensitive information filter.

4Securing AI agent interactions

An AI agent can call tools (APIs, databases). The risks grow because the agent acts.

Control Meaning
Tool-use authorization Give the agent only the tools and permissions it needs; authorize each tool call (for example, with identity and a gateway)
Session isolation Separate each user's session so data and context never mix (AgentCore Runtime runs sessions in isolated environments) [Verify live]
Human-in-the-loop Require a person's approval before sensitive actions (payments, deletions, access changes)

5Protect sensitive content in logs

Monitoring is useful but logs can leak prompts and responses.

Practice Why
Decide what to log Model invocation logging is optional; log only what you need
Mask or redact PII Use CloudWatch Logs data protection or guardrail masking
Encrypt logs with KMS and restrict access Logs are data too
Set retention Do not keep sensitive logs forever
Exam tip

. A VPC endpoint keeps traffic private; a guardrail filters content; an approval step protects sensitive agent actions. Match the control to the risk.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1An application must call Amazon Bedrock without sending traffic over the public internet. What should the developer configure?

  • AA public NAT gateway only
  • BAn internet gateway route
  • CAn interface VPC endpoint for Bedrock
  • DA larger instance
Show the answer

Answer: C. A VPC endpoint (PrivateLink) keeps traffic on the AWS network.

S2A chatbot must never discuss a competitor's pricing. Which Guardrails policy fits?

  • AWord filters only
  • BDenied topics
  • CContextual grounding
  • DPrompt attack filter
Show the answer

Answer: B. Denied topics block subjects defined by meaning.

S3User input could contain "ignore previous instructions". Which control addresses this?

  • APrompt attack filter
  • BS3 Lifecycle
  • CA larger timeout
  • DDynamoDB TTL
Show the answer

Answer: A. The prompt attack filter detects jailbreaks and injections.

S4Model responses sometimes contain customers' phone numbers. Which policy masks them?

  • AContent filters
  • BDenied topics
  • CSensitive information filters
  • DWord filters
Show the answer

Answer: C. Sensitive information filters detect PII and block or mask it.

S5An agent can issue refunds. What is the best safeguard for large refunds?

  • ARemove logging
  • BGive the agent administrator rights
  • CA human approval step before the action
  • DCache the results
Show the answer

Answer: C. Human-in-the-loop approval protects sensitive actions.

S6Logs of AI interactions contain personal data. What should the team do?

  • AMask or redact it, encrypt the logs and restrict access
  • BMake the logs public
  • CKeep them forever
  • DCopy them to a personal laptop
Show the answer

Answer: A. Protect sensitive content in logs with masking, encryption and access control.

6.2 Recall questions

R1Which technology keeps AI traffic off the public internet?

Show the answer

A VPC endpoint (AWS PrivateLink).

R2Name two Guardrails policies.

Show the answer

For example content filters and sensitive information filters (also denied topics, word filters, prompt attack filter, contextual grounding).

R3What does ApplyGuardrail do?

Show the answer

Applies a guardrail to any text without invoking a model.

R4Name two ways to secure an AI agent.

Show the answer

Tool-use authorization, session isolation, human-in-the-loop approval.

R5Is Bedrock model invocation logging on or off by default?

Show the answer

Off by default (it is optional).

R6Is AI governance design on the exam?

Show the answer

No, it is out of scope.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Access enable model access; least-privilege IAM per model
Privacy VPC endpoint, TLS, minimize and redact data
Guardrails content, prompt attack, denied topics, words, sensitive info, grounding; ApplyGuardrail
Agents tool authorization, session isolation, human approval
Logs log only what you need, mask, encrypt, restrict, set retention
